intent: To illustrate the historical trend of U.S. military spending since World War II.

requirements.question: Must the video state or label the full-period net increase from 85 to 580, or is an unlabeled rising line enough?
Must the 2009 maximum of 720 be explicitly marked, or may the peak be inferred visually?
Is the post-2009 decline to 580 required, or can the video end on the peak/overall rise?

units.claim: Over the full period, U.S. military spending rose substantially: from 85 billion in 1950 to 580 billion in 2013, an increase of 495 billion or about 582%.
accept: From 1950 to 2013, spending rose from 85 to 580 billion 2014 USD, +495 billion.
Over the full period, military spending increased by about 582%, or about 6.8× its 1950 level.
The 2013 endpoint is 580 billion, 495 billion above the 1950 value of 85 billion.
units.evidence: The 1950 and 2013 endpoints must be identifiable, labeled, or annotated on the same series.

units.claim: The series reaches its maximum at 720 billion 2014 USD in 2009.
accept: The highest value in the series is 720 billion in 2009.
Spending peaks at 720 billion 2014 USD in 2009.
The maximum occurs in 2009 at 720 billion.
units.evidence: The 2009 data point must be marked or annotated as the maximum.

units.claim: After the 2009 peak, spending fell by 140 billion to 580 billion in 2013, a decline of about 19% from the peak.
accept: After peaking at 720 in 2009, spending fell to 580 by 2013, down 140 billion.
From 2009 to 2013, military spending declined by about 19%, or to about 81% of its peak.
The 2013 endpoint is 140 billion below the 2009 peak.
units.evidence: The 2009 peak and 2013 endpoint must both be visible and linked by a descending segment or annotation.

optional_valid: Threshold crossings: spending first exceeds 500 billion in 1984 (530) and first exceeds 700 billion in 2009 (720).
Post-Cold War decline: from 530 in 1984 to 350 in 1995, a fall of 180 billion, or about 34%.
The series is not monotonic; it has multiple declines, e.g., 1952–1954, 1984–1995, and 2009–2013.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

clip_hardcase.reason: The reference SVG has no explicit data-role=bar mark, so visual-unit reconstruction needs manual review.

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
